comment: D5 slice 4 conformance checklist. Each item applies to the named surfaces (floor, web, kitty) and is tested by a check in conformance_reference.py or by a manual procedure. An implementation passes when every item for its surface passes.

items.requirement: The frame builder produces the golden frame for every case in expected.json.
Every frame keeps the slice 1 invariants: no duplicates, budget and radius held, one focus, no shared angle on a ring, no dangling edges, same frame for reordered input.
An object the viewer cannot read is never drawn, listed or counted in +N more.
An intent on a target outside the frame is refused with target_not_in_frame, and the renderer fetches nothing the frame does not name.
On screen, ring n sits inside ring n+1 and each ring runs clockwise in angle order, after any relaxation.
Keyboard order is the floor's line order, one stop per node.
All five intents are reachable from the keyboard.
A plain click on a node opens it where the pointer can hover; without hover the first click identifies.
Focus is never the plain click: double click, long press, the card's Focus button or f.
identify, identify-link, open and inspect-link never change the frame.
Claimed times are shown as claims, and a time-filtered frame says so.
Open on an edited node goes to the head form so the page follows later edits; open on any other node goes to the object.
The floor lines match floor_expected.json byte for byte for every case.
Labels are sanitised: control, line-breaking and bidi override characters become U+FFFD, so a label cannot drive the terminal or break a line.
With no TTY the output is the floor lines and a newline each, with no escape bytes.
Each probe profile chooses the named surface and mouse mode; every fallback has its reason.
Teardown deletes every image and resets every mode it set, on normal, error and disconnect paths.
Graphics payloads are sent in chunks of at most 4096 base64 characters with m= continuation.
A pointer at a node's centre hits the node, never an edge through it.
Every node in a frame can be reached, by pointer or keyboard.
No frame exceeds 2000 nodes; a cut says so and leaves +N more on the nodes it cut under.
Refocus keeps node identities so the transition can follow each node.
With reduced motion the frame swaps at once and the selection keeps its highlight.
items.procedure: Turn on prefers-reduced-motion (web) or the renderer's reduced-motion setting (terminal), focus a hop-2 node, and record the screen: one change of picture, no intermediate frames, the selected node still highlighted.

items.requirement: The web view carries the floor as a role=tree list beside an aria-hidden canvas, in the same order, with selection shared both ways.
items.procedure: With a screen reader, open notes-replies-first: the tree reads the floor lines in order; selecting a line highlights its node and hovering a node selects its line.

items.requirement: Dimmed context is drawn fainter than bright nodes, and dimmed labels never take cells or space before a bright node's on the same ring.
items.procedure: Render notes-replies-first at the smallest window that shows any label: every bright node with a label has it before any dimmed node on its ring.

items.requirement: A runtime graphics error or failed write moves the view to the floor after a clean reset, with no stray images or modes left.
items.procedure: In kitty, open a frame, then shrink the terminal's image memory (or inject an ENOSPC reply in the harness): the view becomes the floor and the terminal has no placed images and no mouse reporting left on after exit.
